analysis.title: Weekly Mash - 20 Nov 2026
key_insights: Global equities fell hard on the week. Nasdaq is down 7% in five days and has given up all year-to-date gains. The decline has broadened beyond AI winners and precious metals have followed.
The report says the largest company in the world has lost 43% of its value in 5 weeks.
Wilson argues the market faces a worsening liquidity backdrop. Policymakers are adding to a tightening of financial conditions that was already under way because of heavy competition for capital.
The report separates the AI capex wave from the AI productivity payoff. It says the two are distinct and unlikely to emerge at the same time.

The US dollar is retesting highs last seen after the 2024 Trump election win. Hawkish Fed commentary reflects frustration with persistent inflation. Gold and copper have joined the liquidation that has weighed on equities.
Past financial conditions index (FCI) tightenings of 100-150bps produced 10%-20% S&P 500 drawdowns in 2018, 2023 and 2025. The report says the market is now at the lower bound of that range.

The report says the energy price and AI capex pressures that drove the tightening both appear to have turned, so no further Fed action is needed. It also says the Fed likely feels well behind the curve.
Goldman's rule of thumb is that a 100bps FCI tightening of this speed takes 50bps off growth over the next 12 months.

Chip export controls have tightened, which adds uncertainty to the sales path. Nvidia's customer and supply chain financing commitments grew from $366b to $518b this quarter, which reinforced the view that the pace of AI spend is unsustainable.

Wilson links the questions over spend trajectory to Jensen's removal. The report credits him as the architect of the summer plan for Nvidia to work with financial firms to create securitisable compute.

Investors need to separate durable earnings growth from pulled-forward demand or one-time benefits. The report says EPS growth against multiple contraction has defined the last 5 months and that the earnings outlook now matters more than the multiple paid.

Goldman strategists published Global Strategy Paper No.79, 'AI - From Spending to Earnings'. The US equity strategy team's chart shows AI productivity champions diverging from the market and from capex winners over the last 6 weeks.

Wilson sees Europe and the UK as well placed for outsized AI adoption gains because of demographics and services-heavy economies. UK growth has accelerated despite energy headwinds and productivity is improving. The report calls Europe and the UK diversifiers versus staples and expensive defensives.

Hedge fund positioning was all-in on global AI with large capex-winner weightings in 2H 2025 and 1H 2026. That excess has been dramatically cut. The aggregate global long/short ratio of the Prime book is at a record low, with records going back more than 15 years.

Goldman forecasts 18% clean EPS growth for the S&P 500 in 2027, which would mark 5 years of 10%+ earnings growth. Only 1928 and 1999 had 5 consecutive years of double-digit EPS growth. US personal income as a share of GDP has halved in 15 years while corporate profits are at new highs.
Wilson's view is that the market is in the latter stages of a liquidity-induced unwind, but a tightening of this scale could easily mean a 20% pullback.

Short bonds worked as portfolio protection against long equity risk for much of this year. Wilson says that has likely flipped, and long bonds alongside long equities again has merit and correlation value.

sector_views.rationale: Europe benefits most from falling energy prices and the UK and Europe are well placed for AI adoption gains. They are offered as diversifiers versus staples and expensive defensives.

earnings_insights: Goldman forecasts 18% clean S&P 500 EPS growth for 2027 (forecast), which would be a fifth straight year of 10%+ growth.
Nvidia disclosed this quarter that customer and supply chain financing commitments grew from $366b to $518b (reported).

risk_factors: A deteriorating liquidity backdrop and tighter financial conditions could mean a 20% equity pullback.
Uncertainty over the AI capex trajectory after Jensen's removal and tighter chip export controls.
Nvidia's customer and supply chain financing commitments rising to $518b raise doubts about how sustainable the pace of spend is.
AI capex and AI productivity gains may not arrive together.
Persistent inflation is leaving the Fed seen as behind the curve and keeping Fed commentary hawkish.
A stronger dollar and generational high yields reduce the relative appeal of risk assets, gold and copper.
The report notes only 1928 and 1999 saw 5 consecutive years of double-digit EPS growth.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund positioning in global AI and capex winners has been dramatically cut from the all-in levels of 2H 2025 and 1H 2026.
The aggregate global long/short ratio of Goldman's total Prime book is at a new low on its records, which go back more than 15 years.
geopolitical: Tightened chip export controls have created uncertainty around Nvidia's sales path.
A SpaceX rocket catch is cited as an example of accelerating disruption.
